title: Finite smooth level from a normalized orientation
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\ge1$, and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type smooth morphism of Noetherian schemes, of pure relative dimension $d$, with a specified compactification, and with $\ell$ invertible on $Y$. Put $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. Given the actual diagonal-section geometry $G$, an invertibility witness for $\ell^n$ on $X$, and an isomorphism $\alpha:\omega_f\simeq A_X(d)$ shifted by $2d$ satisfying the canonical diagonal/deformation/bundle normalization [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps], there exists a SmoothLevel [def-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-data]. This asserts the finite-level properties only, with no coefficient reduction or quotient cocycle.

source.place: sk-thm-smooth-purity and proof: inverse diagonal orientation followed by the tensor map; sk-prop-sp-orientation.proof.md: diagonal, deformation, vector bundle; sk-lem-sp-reduction.proof.md and sk-lem-sp-reduction-compatibilities.proof.md: counit-defined coefficient comparisons and quotient cocycle. The ordinary-etale Noetherian formulation retains arbitrary ground fields.

proof.text: Use the ordinary smooth tensor-duality isomorphism and tensor alpha inverse to prove gamma invertible on every ordinary input. Derive ordinary gamma naturality from the natural tensor mate and projection map. The constructible essential-image theorem and comparison Tor-interval reflection produce bounded constructible finite-Tor origins. The derived comparison unit, naturality, and the triangle identities show that the actual origin has those properties and its counit is invertible. Thus pro gamma is invertible. Smooth exceptional Tor bounds give exceptional constructibility, then transport by pro gamma gives source constructibility. Construct the natural source comparison by transporting the derived tensor bifunctor comparison and composing the pullback square. Its component calculation is proved with an abstract coefficient category, avoiding unfolding concrete derived tensor structures. Naturality of the inverse origin counit and of ordinary gamma gives pro naturality; the comparison triangle gives the arbitrary-origin equation. On bounded-below source and target, naturality of the fixed compact-support site comparison and the two actual counits gives trace transport. The coefficient unit has Tor interval [0,0]; smooth exceptional bounds and gamma transfer the required unit-degree concentration. Extract graph-normalized sum comparisons from etaleSupportMapCompatibility. Use only the residual geometric dimension-zero map normalization; adjoint uniqueness derives its trace equation. Assemble Level using the original geometry, alpha, and all original maps.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteSmoothLevelOfOrientation
    (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCompactification f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f]
    (hY : ∀ y : Y, IsUnit (ell : Y.presheaf.stalk y))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (G : FiniteRingSectionDeformation.Geometry d
      (pullback.fst f f) (pullback.diagonal f))
    (hX : IsUnit ((ell ^ n : ℕ) : Γ(X, ⊤)))
    (alpha : dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (coefficient ell n)) f ≅
      line (coefficient ell n) (ell ^ n) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) X d)
    (hAlpha : OrientationNormalized (coefficient ell n) (ell ^ n)
      (pow_pos (Fact.out : ell.Prime).pos n) (CharP.cast_eq_zero _ _) f d G hX alpha) :
    Nonempty (Level ell n f d)
